historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal steel revenue growth (volume flat-to-low single digit from MCL7 / North Star debottlenecking, plus price inflation); no historical CAGR is usable because every window's endpoints sit at different points of the steel-spread cycle
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+6.0%) diverges >30% from revenue (+5.3% 5yr / -3.0% 3yr) and EPS (-5.0% 5yr / -5.6% 3yr). The divergence is cycle position, not a data error: FY2021 was an upcycle base (revenue then jumped 47% in FY2022) and FY2023 a post-peak base. Per-share equity compounded at 9.0%/yr over five years because ~65M shares (13%) were bought back.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on OCF - capex - SBC - lease principal (FY2021 773.8 -> FY2026 91.3; FY2023 1,213.8 -> 91.3) and are meaningless as growth signals: FY2021 and FY2023 were spread-driven cash peaks and FY2026 is the peak-capex year of the 6BF reline / MCL7 / NZ EAF program (capex 1,485.7 = 8.9% of revenue vs ~4% mid-cycle). SBC is immaterial (0.15% of revenue) so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF series diverge only by the lease principal, not by SBC. Ten-year average owner FCF FY2017-FY2026 is ~A$690M/yr including the North Star expansion and reline capex, which is the sanity anchor for the base-case mid-cycle owner FCF of ~A$850-900M after the projects.

scenario_narratives.base: BlueScope's earnings are set by regional steel spreads, and FY2027 starts from a tariff-elevated US spread (Section 232 at 50%, US mini-mill benchmark ~US$750/t) that the 1H FY2027 guidance of $860-960M underlying EBIT already reflects. The base case takes that year at face value, then lets spreads mean-revert over FY2028-29 while the completed 6BF reline, MCL7 and NZ EAF lift the mid-cycle margin to ~13% (pre-SBC, post-IFRS-16) versus an 11-year median of 11.8%, crediting roughly 40% of the ~$500M 2030 project EBIT target. Capex falls from 8.9% of revenue at the FY2026 peak to ~4.3% by FY2030, which is what turns a ~A$90M owner-FCF year into ~A$850-900M/yr at mid-cycle. The axes are the durability of the US tariff regime, Chinese export intensity into Asian spreads, and whether the project program earns its ~A$2bn cost.
scenario_narratives.bull: The tariff regime holds for the decade, North Star runs its debottlenecked ~3.3Mtpa at full utilisation with wide US spreads, Australian housing and data-centre construction absorb MCL7's premium COLORBOND/TRUECORE volume, BCP completes its turnaround and the full ~$500M project EBIT uplift lands by 2030. Mid-cycle margin 14.5%, still well short of the FY2021-22 upcycle, and revenue compounds ~3.5% nominal. The $3.00/share CY2027 distribution is sustainable rather than debt-funded.
scenario_narratives.bear: Section 232 is rolled back or carved out in a trade deal, US spreads fall back toward FY2025 levels, and persistent Chinese overcapacity keeps Asian benchmark spreads near US$200/t; revenue drops 6% in FY2028 and the mid-cycle margin settles at 11%, with reline/EAF commissioning running late and over budget so capex stays elevated. The CY2027 $3.00/share distribution has to be funded from the A$1.5bn net-debt ceiling while free cash flow is thin, and a new CEO faces simultaneous execution issues at BCP, NZ Steel and Port Kembla.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical steel producer is worth its mid-cycle owner cash flow, not its best or worst year. The model deliberately does not extrapolate FY2026 (tariff-elevated US spreads at peak reline capex), FY2025 (trough, BCP impairment) or FY2022 (record spreads). It charges leases once (in the flows, with lease liabilities excluded from net debt), NCI once (as an 8% leakage on EBIT, with the NCI stock not deducted), SBC once (expensed at 0.15% of revenue with a flat share count), and risk once (in the scenario flows and weights, not the discount rate). The terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF because the market has never paid a compounder multiple for a steelmaker.
key_risks_to_valuation: US Section 232 tariff rollback or carve-out: North Star's FY2026 EBIT of $805M vs $267M in FY2025 is largely a tariff-spread effect; the bear case is a 30% weight for this reason
Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of EBITDA margin is roughly A$190M of EBITDA and ~A$2.5-3/share of value; the 13% base mid-cycle assumes ~40% of the $500M 2030 project target is delivered

Capex normalisation: the valuation depends on capex falling from 8.9% of revenue to ~4.3% after the reline/MCL7/EAF program; sustained project overruns or a new wave of decarbonisation capex (NeoSmelt, EAF pathways) would defer the FCF harvest
Chinese steel overcapacity and export intensity structurally capping Asian and Australian export spreads
Combined 34% tax+NCI leakage: a permanently lower underlying tax rate (e.g. more US-weighted earnings at 21%) would add value; a higher NCI share of profit from the NS BlueScope JV would subtract

Unmodelled upside: ~1,200 ha of surplus industrial land (West Dapto, Western Port) with no carrying value in the bridge; unmodelled downside: the NCI's 50% share of the consolidated NS BlueScope JV cash is not deducted

Balance sheet: net debt (company basis) rose from A$28M to A$600M in FY2026 funding $3.00/share of distributions ahead of project completion; a further $3.00/share is targeted for CY2027 against a A$1.5bn ceiling

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average 441,452,116 (FY2026 AR note, line 7656) vs 438.3M basic on issue; held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. Share rights are small (~3M) and BlueScope has historically satisfied them with on-market purchases. Buybacks are the mechanism that keeps the count flat; they are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payment expense' 24.3 (line 6516); no separate equity-award tax line disclosed, no combined figure published, so the SoCE figure is used as-is
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-22T03:48:39Z (ASX regular session, intraday; Yahoo chart meta)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: Australian 10y government bond ~4.4%, ERP ~5.5%, equity beta ~1.2 for a global steel producer gives cost of equity ~11%; after-tax cost of debt ~4% on investment-grade (S&P/Moody's) facilities; ~90/10 equity/debt weights at market values (gross debt A$1.2bn vs A$13bn market cap) gives ~10.2%, rounded to 10.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, the Section 232 tariff dependency and project execution are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (section 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full FY2026 lease cash cost of 164.4 (principal 124.3 from financing, line 6602; interest 40.1, line 9205) = 0.99% of revenue is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (1.0%). Lease liabilities of 585.7 are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt: net_debt = borrowings 1,181.3 (79.9 current + 1,101.4 non-current) - cash 1,167.0 = 14.3. The company's own 'net debt' of 600.0 includes leases (14.3 + 585.7 = 600.0, ties exactly) and must not be used with this treatment. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: 692.9 total - ~124 ROU (approximated by the principal repayment) = ~569 = 3.4% of revenue in FY0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Non-controlling interests (chiefly Nippon Steel's 50% of NS BlueScope Coated Products) took 100.7 of FY2026 profit (line 6361), ~8% of underlying EBIT (142.5 in FY2024 = 10.6%, 127.3 in FY2023 = 7.9%). The cash_tax_rate_path of 34% is a COMBINED leakage rate: ~26% mid-cycle cash tax (underlying ETR 25.4% FY2024, 27.5% FY2025, 20.9% FY2026 with the non-assessable TBSL gain; cash taxes paid 205 on PBT 1,136 in FY2026) plus ~8% NCI share of EBIT. The NCI stock of 587.2 is NOT deducted in the bridge. Calibration: FY0 component NOPAT on the FY2026 actuals = (1,894.4 + 24.3 EBITDA pre-SBC - 24.3 SBC - 164.4 lease - 569 D&A ex-ROU) x 0.66 = ~766 vs reported attributable NPAT 802.0 / underlying NPAT 851, within non-operating noise (interest income 28.5, TBSL gain).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, with the section 7 cyclical/non-US adaptations, on a MID-CYCLE basis. BlueScope is an operating company (integrated steelmaker + coated building products), so the owner-FCF engine is the right family; the adaptation is that neither FY2026 (tariff-elevated US spreads, peak reline capex) nor FY2025 (trough, BCP impairment) nor FY2022 (record spreads, 23% EBITDA margin) is a repeatable base. Margins are anchored to the 11-year EBITDA-margin record (FY2016-FY2026 median 11.8%, mean 13.0%; post-IFRS-16 FY2020-26 mean 12.7%, median 11.5%) and the forward path starts from the 1H FY2027 guidance year (underlying EBIT $860-960M) then fades to mid-cycle by year 4-5 with a partial credit for the ~$500M-by-2030 project EBIT target. EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: the engine's ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC and POST-IFRS-16 (i.e. before the SBC and lease charges the engine deducts); FY2026 actual on that basis = (1,894.4 reported EBITDA + 24.3 SBC) / 16,662.6 = 11.5%. INTEREST INCOME: not stripped (interest_income = 0 in the deduction) because the company is in net debt (A$14.3M ex-lease, A$600M incl. leases); the 28.5 of interest received is left in the flows and cash is netted in the bridge at face. LAST_FCF: 91.3 = reported FCF 239.9 (OCF 1,725.6 - capex 1,485.7) - SBC 24.3 - lease principal 124.3 - interest income 0; the lease principal deduction is the treatment-(B) counterpart to excluding lease liabilities from net debt, and the figure is a peak-capex year (6BF reline, MCL7, NZ EAF) that the component build does not extrapolate. Interest income is small and the company is a net borrower, so no matching-asset issue arises. SURPLUS LAND: ~1,200 ha of surplus industrial land (West Dapto, Western Port) is a real non-operating asset with no disclosed carrying value in the context; it is NOT in the bridge and is listed as unmodelled upside. NCI SHARE OF JV CASH: consolidated cash includes the NS BlueScope Coated Products JV's liquidity ('$775M liquidity in the JV', which includes undrawn facilities); the 50% NCI share of the JV's cash component is not deducted in the bridge and is noted as a modest overstatement risk (<A$1/share). PRICE: intraday ASX print; replace at the next regular close if it moves materially.
inputs.sanity_multiples: At A$29.77 the market cap is ~A$13.1bn; EV ex-lease ~A$13.2bn; EV incl. leases ~A$13.7bn. On FY2026 reported (post-IFRS-16) EBITDA of 1,894 the lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA is ~7.2x; on the lease-consistent basis (ex-lease EV over EBITDA less 164 lease cash = 1,730) it is ~7.6x. Against the base-case mid-cycle EBITDA (~13% x ~A$19bn = ~A$2.5bn, post-IFRS-16 ~2.5bn) it is ~5.3x.

bear.margin_note: Section 232 is rolled back or carved out in a trade deal during FY2028, US spreads fall back toward the FY2025 level, Chinese export intensity keeps Asian spreads depressed, and the projects deliver late/under target: revenue -6% in FY2028 and a 11.0% mid-cycle margin (between the FY2023-24 11.5-11.8% and the FY2025 trough 6.2%). Capex stays higher for longer on reline/EAF overruns.

base.growth_note: FY2027 +5% on higher realised spreads (US mini-mill benchmark ~US$750/t per 1H guidance) and stronger domestic volumes; FY2028 flat as spreads normalise; 3% then 2.5% nominal thereafter (MCL7 240ktpa and North Star ~300ktpa debottlenecking volumes plus price inflation).
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC, post-IFRS-16 basis. FY2027 14.0% reconciles to 1H FY2027 underlying EBIT guidance of $860-960M plus a softer 2H (year-1 component EBIT ~A$1.65bn). Fades to 12.25% in FY2029 as US spreads mean-revert, then recovers to a 13.0% mid-cycle from FY2032: the 11-year record (median 11.8%, post-IFRS-16 mean 12.7%) plus ~1pp for the FY2027 $150M net cost program and roughly 40% of the ~$500M 2030 project EBIT target.
base.capex_note: FY2027 6.9% (~A$1.2bn) with the 6BF reline completing early CY2027 and MCL7/NZ EAF ramping; FY2028 5.2%; 4.3% steady state (~A$800-850M), slightly above D&A of 4.0% to reflect cost inflation on replacement.
base.da_note: Ex right-of-use depreciation (3.4% in FY2026), rising to 4.0% as the ~A$2bn reline/MCL7/EAF program is commissioned and depreciated.
base.tax_note: 34% is a combined cash-tax (~26%) plus NCI-leakage (~8% of EBIT) rate; see inputs.nci_treatment.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: receivables + inventory exceed payables by ~15% of revenue, so growth consumes cash; -15% capture on the revenue change.
base.terminal_note: 12x owner-FCF cap for a cyclical steel producer (Gordon at 10%/2.5% would be 13.7x); the cap binds.

bull.margin_note: Section 232 at 50% persists through the decade, North Star runs the debottlenecked capacity at full utilisation, the full ~$500M 2030 project EBIT uplift is delivered and BCP completes its turnaround: mid-cycle 14.5% (still below the FY2018/FY2021 16-17% and far below the FY2022 23% peak).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default because the FY2026-27 earnings step-up rests on a single policy lever (US Section 232 at 50%) that one trade deal can reverse, and because Chinese export intensity has no visible resolution; this is a single-regulator dependency, not ordinary cyclicality. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: tariffs persisting for a decade, the full ~$500M project target being delivered on time, and BCP's turnaround completing. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
